generic.Defined scope/population: Every affected line of business and the named senior underwriters reviewing the coverage design pack.
generic.In-scope period: The coverage design version circulated at least 5 business days before the peer review session.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Each comment row carries commenter, clause reference, accept or reject decision and action owner.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Comment count in the review sheet matches comments returned by every circulated reviewer.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Signed peer-review sheet attached to the coverage design version in the product repository with date.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Open peer-review actions logged with owner and due date and closed before CUO sign-off.
generic.Test population: All peer comments raised on the coverage design version submitted for sign-off.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: Fail if any affected line lacks a named reviewer or any comment lacks a disposition.
generic.Exception handling path: Unresolved comments escalate to the Insurance Product Dev Lead and hold the sign-off submission.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: Peer-review sheet complete with reviewer names, dispositioned comments and zero open actions.
generic.Evidence location: Coverage review sheet and signed peer-review sheet in the SharePoint product design library.

steps.title: Assemble the coverage design review pack in SharePoint
sop: Pull the current coverage design version, limits table and eligibility tiers from the document management repository.
Compile them into a single review pack and mark the version number and date on the cover page.
Save the pack to the SharePoint peer review folder for the product.
Done when the versioned review pack is saved in the SharePoint peer review folder.
verify: Open the pack and confirm the version number matches the current coverage design version.
Pass when the pack contains design, limits and eligibility content at one stated version.

steps.title: Name the senior underwriter reviewers per line of business
sop: List every line of business affected by the coverage design.
Name at least one senior underwriter reviewer against each line in the review sheet.
Confirm each named reviewer is available for the review session date.
Done when every affected line has a named and available reviewer recorded.
verify: Cross-check the reviewer list against the affected lines list.
Pass when no affected line of business is left without a named reviewer.

steps.title: Circulate the pack from SharePoint five business days ahead
sop: Share the SharePoint pack link with every named reviewer at least 5 business days before the session.
State in the invitation which sections each reviewer must assess and the comment return date.
Record the circulation date and recipient list in the review sheet.
Done when the circulation date and recipients are recorded and the lead time is met.
verify: Compare the recorded circulation date against the session date.
Pass when the gap is 5 business days or more for every reviewer.

steps.title: Run the review session over the four mandated coverage topics
sop: Walk the session through insuring agreement wording, exclusion set, sub-limits and eligibility tiers in turn.
Confirm out loud that each reviewer has assessed all four topics for their line.
Capture challenges to wording and tiers as they are raised rather than after the session.
Done when all four topics have been covered and reviewer assessment is confirmed.
verify: Read back the session record against the four mandated topics.
Pass when each topic shows a recorded assessment from every attending reviewer.

steps.title: Log every comment and disposition in the coverage review sheet
sop: Enter each comment in the review sheet with commenter name and the clause reference it targets.
Record the accept or reject decision agreed in session against every comment.
Raise any comment needing work as an action with a named owner and due date.
Done when no comment row is missing a commenter, clause reference or decision.
verify: Filter the review sheet for blank decision, commenter or clause reference cells.
Pass when the filter returns no rows.

steps.title: Drive open review actions to closure before sign-off
sop: Chase each action owner against the due date recorded in the review sheet.
Confirm the coverage design edit for each action has been applied before closing it.
Update the action status to closed with the date and the applied change noted.
Done when no peer-review action remains in Open status.
verify: Filter the action list for Open status on the version going to CUO sign-off.
Pass when zero actions remain open on that version.

steps.title: Attach the signed peer-review sheet to the design version
sop: Obtain the Insurance Product Dev Lead signature on the completed review sheet.
Attach the signed sheet to the coverage design version in the document management repository.
Tag the attachment with the design version number and the review date.
Done when the signed sheet is attached and tagged against the correct design version.
verify: Open the design version record and check the attachment list.
Pass when the signed peer-review sheet is present and tagged to that version.

generic.Defined scope/population: Every candidate peril and every target customer segment proposed for the new product.
generic.In-scope period: The product specification version being taken forward into pricing and forms drafting.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Each peril has an in-scope or out-of-scope decision and each segment has class, geography and size band.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Peril and segment counts in the specification match the counts in the appetite confirmation.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Versioned product specification and dated appetite owner confirmation held in SharePoint.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Segments overlapping the no-write list logged and removed or escalated with a written decision.
generic.Test population: All perils and segments listed in the product specification.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: Fail if any peril lacks a decision or any segment appears on the prohibited-risk list.
generic.Exception handling path: Appetite conflicts route to the Insurance Product Dev Lead before the specification is issued.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: Perils decisioned, segments defined by class, geography and size, and appetite confirmed in writing.
generic.Evidence location: Product specification and appetite confirmation in the SharePoint product design library.

steps.title: Build the candidate peril list in the product specification
sop: List every peril the product could cover, drawn from market wordings and the original product concept.
Enter each peril as its own row in the specification held in SharePoint.
Leave the decision column blank at this stage so no peril is presumed in scope.
Done when every candidate peril appears as a discrete row in the specification.
verify: Count the peril rows against the source wording and concept list.
Pass when no candidate peril from the sources is missing from the specification.

steps.title: Record an in-scope or out-of-scope decision for each peril
sop: Decide each peril in or out of scope with the Insurance Product Dev Lead.
Record the decision and a one-line reason against the peril row.
Flag perils that depend on a reinsurance or appetite decision as pending with an owner.
Done when every peril row carries an explicit in-scope or out-of-scope decision.
verify: Filter the peril table for blank decision cells.
Pass when the filter returns no rows.

steps.title: Define target segments by class code, geography and size band
sop: Define each target segment using industry class code, geography and revenue or size band.
Avoid narrative descriptions so the segment can later be coded as a system rule.
Record each segment as a row in the specification with all three attributes populated.
Done when every target segment carries class code, geography and size band.
verify: Filter the segment table for any row missing one of the three attributes.
Pass when every segment row has class code, geography and size band populated.

steps.title: Screen segments against the no-write and prohibited-risk lists
sop: Retrieve the current no-write and prohibited-risk lists from the document management repository.
Compare every target segment class code and geography against both lists.
Remove overlapping segments or log the overlap for an explicit appetite decision.
Done when no target segment remains that overlaps either list without a logged decision.
verify: Re-run the comparison against the current list version.
Pass when no target segment matches an entry on the no-write or prohibited-risk list.

steps.title: Confirm loss data or an agreed proxy exists for each in-scope peril
sop: For each in-scope peril, identify the internal loss data or external proxy basis available.
Record the data source and period against the peril row in the specification.
Refer perils with no data and no agreed proxy back for an in or out decision.
Done when every in-scope peril names a loss data source or an agreed proxy basis.
verify: Check each in-scope peril row for a populated data source field.
Pass when no in-scope peril is carried into pricing without a data or proxy basis.

steps.title: Obtain written appetite confirmation and version the specification
sop: Send the final peril and segment tables to the appetite owner for written confirmation.
Obtain confirmation that perils and segments sit inside the risk appetite statement.
Save the confirmation alongside the specification and increment the specification version.
Done when the dated appetite confirmation is filed against the issued specification version.
verify: Open the specification record and check for the attached appetite confirmation.
Pass when a dated written confirmation is attached to the issued version.

generic.Defined scope/population: Every deductible, sub-limit, coinsurance and policy limit option offered on each coverage part.
generic.In-scope period: The limits-and-retentions table version linked to the current coverage design package.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Each option row shows coverage part, value, default or optional or referral flag and pricing basis.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Option count in the table matches the options named in the coverage design package.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Versioned limits-and-retentions table stored in the document management repository with date.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Limit options above the treaty retention logged with the referral rule that governs them.
generic.Test population: All deductible, sub-limit, coinsurance and limit options in the table.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: Fail if any option lacks a flag or exceeds treaty retention without a documented referral rule.
generic.Exception handling path: Options the actuary cannot price route back to the Insurance Product Dev Lead for removal or pricing work.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: Complete option table with min and max limits per coverage part and confirmed priceability.
generic.Evidence location: Limits-and-retentions table in SharePoint linked to the coverage design package.

steps.title: Tabulate every retention and limit option in SharePoint
sop: Create the limits-and-retentions table with one row per option in the SharePoint product design library.
Enter every deductible option, sub-limit, coinsurance percentage and policy limit the product will offer.
Record the coverage part each option applies to on the same row.
Done when every offered option appears as a row against its coverage part.
verify: Compare the table rows against the options named in the coverage design package.
Pass when every option in the design package appears in the table.

steps.title: State minimum and maximum limits per coverage part
sop: For each coverage part, state the minimum limit and the maximum limit the product will write.
Record both values in the table header row for that coverage part.
Check the maximum is consistent with the product concept and the appetite statement.
Done when every coverage part shows a stated minimum and maximum limit.
verify: Check each coverage part block for populated minimum and maximum values.
Pass when no coverage part is missing either bound.

steps.title: Flag limit options above the reinsurance treaty retention
sop: Retrieve the current treaty retention by coverage part from the document management repository.
Compare every limit option against the retention and flag those that exceed it.
Write the referral rule that must apply to each flagged option.
Done when every option above retention carries a written referral rule.
verify: Filter the table for options above retention with a blank referral rule.
Pass when the filter returns no rows.

steps.title: Confirm each retention option is priceable with the actuary
sop: Review each deductible, sub-limit and coinsurance option for an available factor basis.
Record agreed, agreed with proxy or not priceable against each option row.
Return options marked not priceable to the analyst for removal or redefinition.
Done when every option carries a recorded priceability decision.
verify: Filter the table for options with no recorded priceability decision.
Pass when every option shows an actuarial priceability decision.

steps.title: Mark each option as default, optional or referral
sop: Set exactly one default option per coverage part and per option type.
Mark the remaining options optional or referral according to the agreed underwriting treatment.
Check no coverage part has two defaults or none for a given option type.
Done when every option row carries a default, optional or referral flag.
verify: Group the table by coverage part and option type and count the defaults.
Pass when each group has exactly one default and no unflagged rows.

steps.title: Version the table and link it to the coverage design package
sop: Increment the table version and stamp it with the date and product code.
Store the versioned table in the document management repository.
Link the table to the current coverage design package record.
Done when the versioned table is stored and linked to the design package.
verify: Open the coverage design package record and follow the limits table link.
Pass when the link resolves to the current versioned limits-and-retentions table.

generic.Defined scope/population: Every coverage part requiring an insuring agreement in the new product wording.
generic.In-scope period: The draft wording version circulated to Legal before exclusions drafting begins.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Each insuring agreement names the trigger, the covered event and the promise to pay.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Insuring agreement count matches the coverage part count in the approved perils list.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Versioned draft wording stored in the document management repository with the drafting date.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Clauses that deviate from bureau wording logged as company deviation with a written rationale.
generic.Test population: All insuring agreements and all capitalised terms used within them.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: Fail if any capitalised term is undefined or any peril is granted that was scoped out.
generic.Exception handling path: New wording with no bureau precedent routes to Legal Counsel before it is carried forward.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: Insuring agreement per coverage part with clause-level source annotation and complete definitions.
generic.Evidence location: Draft wording and clause source annotation log in the document management repository.

steps.title: List the coverage parts requiring insuring agreements
sop: Read the approved perils and coverage scope from the product specification in SharePoint.
List each coverage part that needs its own insuring agreement.
Confirm the list with the Insurance Product Dev Lead before drafting starts.
Done when the confirmed coverage part list is recorded in the drafting file.
verify: Compare the coverage part list against the approved perils list.
Pass when every approved coverage part appears on the drafting list.

steps.title: Draft the insuring agreement for each coverage part
sop: Draft each insuring agreement naming the trigger, the covered event and the promise to pay.
Keep each agreement to its own coverage part rather than combining parts in one clause.
Save the draft in the document management repository under the product wording folder.
Done when every listed coverage part has a drafted insuring agreement.
verify: Read each agreement for a stated trigger, covered event and promise to pay.
Pass when all three elements are present in every insuring agreement.

steps.title: Annotate each clause with its source
sop: Mark each clause as bureau or ISO standard, company deviation or new wording.
Record the bureau form reference where standard wording has been adopted.
Write the rationale for each company deviation and each piece of new wording.
Done when every clause carries a source annotation and deviations carry a rationale.
verify: Scan the annotation column for blank entries.
Pass when no clause is left without a source annotation.

steps.title: Define every capitalised term in the Definitions section
sop: Extract every capitalised term used in the insuring agreements into a term list.
Draft or adopt a definition for each term in the Definitions section.
Check the defined wording is used consistently wherever the term appears.
Done when every capitalised term used has a matching definition.
verify: Compare the extracted term list against the Definitions section entries.
Pass when no capitalised term used in an insuring agreement is missing from Definitions.

steps.title: Check the agreements against the approved perils list
sop: Read each insuring agreement against the approved in-scope and out-of-scope peril decisions.
Flag any wording that grants a peril recorded as out of scope.
Return flagged wording to the Policy Forms Specialist for amendment before Legal review.
Done when no insuring agreement grants an out-of-scope peril.
verify: Re-read the amended agreements against the peril decision table.
Pass when every granted peril appears as in scope on the approved list.

steps.title: Circulate the draft agreements to Legal in SharePoint
sop: Version the draft insuring agreements and save them in the SharePoint review folder.
Share the version with Legal Counsel and state the review return date.
Confirm exclusions drafting is held until Legal has responded.
Done when Legal has the versioned draft and the circulation is recorded.
verify: Check the review folder for the circulated version and the recorded send date.
Pass when the circulation is recorded before any exclusions drafting starts.

generic.Defined scope/population: Every eligibility criterion and every risk classification tier proposed for the new product.
generic.In-scope period: The eligibility and tier tables version going into the coverage design package.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Each criterion is a pass or fail test and each tier states entry criteria and boundary values.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Tier count in the eligibility table matches the tier count carried into the rating plan.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Versioned eligibility and tier tables with the Compliance initial and date held in SharePoint.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Classification variables flagged as restricted in a state logged and removed or state-limited.
generic.Test population: All eligibility criteria, tier definitions and classification variables.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: Fail if any criterion is narrative rather than testable or any variable is prohibited in a target state.
generic.Exception handling path: Prohibited or restricted variables route to Compliance Analyst for removal before packaging.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: Pass or fail eligibility rules, tier boundaries defined and every tier mapped to a rating factor.
generic.Evidence location: Eligibility and tier tables in the SharePoint product design library.

steps.title: Write eligibility criteria as codable pass or fail tests
sop: Convert each eligibility requirement into a test with a named attribute, operator and value.
Remove narrative guidance wording that cannot be coded as a system rule.
Record each test as a row in the eligibility table in SharePoint.
Done when every eligibility criterion is expressed as a pass or fail test.
verify: Read each criterion and attempt to state it as a rule with attribute, operator and value.
Pass when every criterion resolves to a testable rule without judgement.

steps.title: Define each risk classification tier and its boundaries
sop: Define each tier with its entry criteria and the numeric boundary against the adjacent tier.
Check that adjacent tier boundaries meet without gap or overlap.
Record the tier definitions in the tier table alongside the eligibility table.
Done when every tier carries entry criteria and stated boundary values.
verify: Walk the boundary values from the lowest tier to the highest.
Pass when the boundaries are continuous with no gap or overlap.

steps.title: Screen classification variables against restricted rating factors by state
sop: Retrieve the prohibited and restricted rating factor list by state from the repository.
Compare every proposed classification variable against that list for each target state.
Mark each hit as remove or restrict to named states and record the decision.
Done when every proposed variable has been screened and every hit dispositioned.
verify: Re-run the screen against the current restricted factor list.
Pass when no prohibited or restricted characteristic remains as a classification variable.

steps.title: Map every tier to at least one rating factor
sop: Compare the tier list against the rating factors planned in the rating methodology.
Record the rating factor that each tier drives against the tier row.
Escalate any tier with no rating factor as unpriceable and agree removal or a factor.
Done when every tier names at least one rating factor.
verify: Filter the tier table for rows with no rating factor recorded.
Pass when the filter returns no rows.

steps.title: Obtain the Compliance initial on the eligibility and tier tables
sop: Review the final eligibility and tier tables against the screening results.
Initial and date both tables to record Compliance acceptance.
Note any state-limited variable as a condition on the initialled tables.
Done when both tables carry a dated Compliance initial.
verify: Open the tables and check for the Compliance initial and date.
Pass when both tables are initialled and dated before packaging.

steps.title: Issue the tables into the coverage design package
sop: Version the initialled eligibility and tier tables with product code and date.
Add them to the coverage design package in the document management repository.
Notify the Insurance Product Dev Lead that the tables are in the package.
Done when the versioned tables are part of the current coverage design package.
verify: Open the coverage design package and locate both tables.
Pass when the package contains the initialled and versioned tables.

generic.Defined scope/population: Every endorsement, extension, rider and optional coverage module drafted for the product.
generic.In-scope period: The endorsement drafting cycle for the current approved coverage design version.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Each endorsement carries form number, edition date, attachment rule and base form clause amended.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Endorsement index entry count matches the number of drafted endorsement documents.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Drafted endorsements and the endorsement index stored with edition dates in the repository.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Endorsements broadening coverage logged with the pricing factor or removed from the set.
generic.Test population: All drafted endorsements, extensions and riders in the endorsement index.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: Fail if any endorsement lacks a form number or grants coverage outside the approved perils list.
generic.Exception handling path: Coverage-broadening wording routes to Legal Counsel and the actuary before it is indexed.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: Unique form number, edition date and attachment rule on every endorsement in the index.
generic.Evidence location: Endorsement drafts and endorsement index in the document management repository.

steps.title: Draft each endorsement as standalone amending wording
sop: Draft each endorsement, extension and rider as standalone wording in the repository.
Name the base form and the specific clause the endorsement amends in the opening line.
Avoid restating coverage already granted in the base form.
Done when every endorsement expressly amends a named base form clause.
verify: Read each endorsement opening line for the named base form and clause.
Pass when no endorsement restates coverage instead of amending a clause.

steps.title: Assign form numbers and edition dates
sop: Assign a form number to each endorsement using the company numbering convention.
Set the edition date to the drafting cycle date for each endorsement.
Check no form number already exists on another in-force form.
Done when every endorsement has a unique form number and an edition date.
verify: Sort the form numbers and look for duplicates or blanks.
Pass when every endorsement has a unique number and a populated edition date.

steps.title: Classify each endorsement as mandatory, optional or state-specific
sop: Record for each endorsement whether it is mandatory, optional or state-specific.
Record which base form it attaches to and under what condition it attaches.
Confirm state-specific endorsements name the states they apply to.
Done when every endorsement carries a classification and an attachment rule.
verify: Filter the endorsement list for blank classification or attachment rule.
Pass when the filter returns no rows.

steps.title: Check endorsements against the approved perils and limits
sop: Compare the coverage granted by each endorsement against the approved perils and limits table.
Flag any endorsement that broadens coverage beyond the approved position.
Route each flagged endorsement for a pricing factor decision or amendment.
Done when no endorsement broadens coverage without a recorded pricing factor.
verify: Re-check the flagged endorsements against the pricing factor decisions.
Pass when every broadening endorsement names a corresponding rating factor.

steps.title: Obtain Legal review of the endorsement wording
sop: Review each endorsement for legal effect and consistency with the base form.
Record findings with the endorsement form number and the required change.
Confirm closure of each finding before the endorsement enters the index.
Done when every Legal finding on the endorsement set is closed.
verify: Check the Legal finding log for open items against endorsement form numbers.
Pass when no finding remains open on an indexed endorsement.

steps.title: Build the endorsement index in the repository
sop: Build the index listing form number, title, edition date and attachment rule for every endorsement.
Cross-check the index entry count against the number of drafted documents.
Store the index with the endorsement set in the document management repository.
Done when the index lists every drafted endorsement with all four attributes.
verify: Compare the index row count to the drafted endorsement document count.
Pass when the counts match and no index row is missing an attribute.

generic.Defined scope/population: Every exclusion, policy condition and definition drafted for the new product wording.
generic.In-scope period: The wording drafting cycle following Legal clearance of the insuring agreements.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Each exclusion is a lettered clause stating what is excluded and any write-back.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Defined term count matches the terms actually used across all coverage parts.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Versioned exclusions, conditions and definitions draft dated in the document management repository.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Exclusions prohibited or restricted in a state flagged to the state-variation workstream with an owner.
generic.Test population: All drafted exclusions, conditions and definitions.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: Fail if any exclusion lacks a rationale or contradicts coverage granted elsewhere.
generic.Exception handling path: Exclusions without bureau precedent or reinsurance basis route to Legal Counsel for decision.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: Lettered exclusions with rationale and write-backs, full condition set and consistent definitions.
generic.Evidence location: Draft wording and exclusion rationale log in the document management repository.

steps.title: Draft each exclusion as a lettered clause
sop: Draft each exclusion as its own lettered clause in the wording document.
State plainly what the clause excludes and set out any write-back.
Avoid bundling unrelated exclusions into a single clause.
Done when every exclusion stands as a lettered clause with its write-back stated.
verify: Read the exclusions section clause by clause.
Pass when each exclusion is separately lettered with its scope and write-back clear.

steps.title: Record the basis for every exclusion
sop: Record for each exclusion whether it rests on bureau precedent, reinsurance requirement or underwriting rationale.
Cite the bureau form or treaty clause reference where one applies.
Write the underwriting rationale where no external basis exists.
Done when every exclusion carries one of the three recorded bases.
verify: Filter the exclusion log for rows with no recorded basis.
Pass when the filter returns no rows.

steps.title: Draft the policy conditions set
sop: Draft conditions covering notice of loss, cooperation, cancellation, subrogation and dispute resolution.
Check each condition against the base coverage structure so it operates on all coverage parts.
Save the conditions section into the versioned wording document.
Done when all five mandated condition topics are drafted.
verify: Check the conditions section against the five mandated topics.
Pass when no mandated condition topic is missing.

steps.title: Align definitions used in exclusions and conditions
sop: Extract every defined term used in the exclusions and conditions sections.
Confirm each term appears in Definitions and is used the same way in every coverage part.
Amend inconsistent usage rather than adding a second definition.
Done when every term used is defined once and used consistently.
verify: Compare the extracted terms against the Definitions section and their usage.
Pass when no term is undefined and no term carries two meanings.

steps.title: Check exclusions against granted coverage
sop: Read each exclusion against the insuring agreements and endorsements that grant coverage.
Flag any exclusion that removes coverage the product intends to grant.
Agree the amendment or the write-back needed to resolve each conflict.
Done when no exclusion contradicts an insuring agreement or endorsement.
verify: Re-read the amended exclusions against the granting clauses.
Pass when no conflict remains between an exclusion and granted coverage.

steps.title: Flag state-prohibited exclusions to the variation workstream
sop: Compare each exclusion against the state prohibited and modified wording matrix.
Flag exclusions that are prohibited or must be modified in named states.
Log each flag to the state-variation workstream with the state and required treatment.
Done when every state-affected exclusion is logged to the variation workstream.
verify: Check the variation workstream log against the flagged exclusions.
Pass when every flagged exclusion appears with its state and required treatment.

generic.Defined scope/population: Every Legal, Compliance and underwriting comment raised on the prior coverage design version.
generic.In-scope period: The comment log covering the review round on the version being revised.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Each comment row shows commenter, clause, disposition and rationale where rejected or deferred.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Dispositioned comment count equals the total comments received in the review round.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: New design version with redline and change summary stored and dated in the repository.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Rejected and deferred comments logged with rationale and routed back to the commenter.
generic.Test population: All comments in the Legal, Compliance and underwriting comment log.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: Fail if any comment has no disposition or the new version has no redline against the prior version.
generic.Exception handling path: Disputed rejections escalate to Legal Counsel before the revised version is issued.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: Every comment dispositioned and a new version issued with redline and change summary.
generic.Evidence location: Comment log, redline and change summary in the SharePoint product design library.

steps.title: Consolidate the review comments into one log
sop: Collect the Legal, Compliance and underwriting comments into a single log in SharePoint.
Give each comment a unique reference and record the commenter and clause it targets.
Reconcile the log count against the comments received from each reviewer.
Done when all comments from the three sources sit in one referenced log.
verify: Compare the log count against each reviewer's returned comment count.
Pass when the totals reconcile with no missing comment.

steps.title: Disposition each comment accept, reject or defer
sop: Work the log line by line and mark each comment accepted, rejected or deferred.
Agree contested dispositions with the Insurance Product Dev Lead before recording them.
Leave no comment without a recorded decision.
Done when every comment row carries an accept, reject or defer disposition.
verify: Filter the log for rows with no disposition.
Pass when the filter returns no rows.

steps.title: Record rationale and return rejected and deferred comments
sop: Write a rationale against every rejected and deferred comment.
Send the rationale back to the commenter who raised the comment.
Record the date the rationale was returned in the log.
Done when every rejected or deferred comment has a rationale and a return date.
verify: Filter for rejected or deferred rows with no rationale or return date.
Pass when the filter returns no rows.

steps.title: Apply the accepted changes to the coverage design
sop: Apply each accepted comment to the coverage design document in the repository.
Mark the log row applied with the clause reference of the edit made.
Keep the prior version intact so a redline can be produced.
Done when every accepted comment is applied and marked in the log.
verify: Sample accepted comments and locate the corresponding edit in the document.
Pass when each sampled accepted comment has a matching edit.

steps.title: Re-check cross-references after the edits
sop: Re-read cross-references between insuring agreements, exclusions and definitions after the edits.
Flag any reference that now points at a renumbered or deleted clause.
Have the flagged references corrected before the version is issued.
Done when every cross-reference resolves to an existing clause.
verify: Walk the cross-reference list against the revised document.
Pass when no cross-reference points to a missing clause.

steps.title: Issue the new version with redline and change summary
sop: Produce a redline of the revised design against the prior version.
Write a change summary at the front listing each accepted change.
Increment the version number and publish to the SharePoint design library.
Done when the new version is published with its redline and change summary.
verify: Open the issued version and check for the redline and change summary.
Pass when both are present and the version number has incremented.

generic.Defined scope/population: The final coverage terms, limits table, eligibility tiers and endorsement index going to the CUO.
generic.In-scope period: The coverage design version submitted for Chief Underwriting Officer sign-off.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Sign-off pack names the document version, date and every prerequisite review with its status.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Pack contents list matches the documents actually attached to the sign-off submission.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Executed CUO sign-off filed with the approved version and date in the governance record.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Conditions or carve-outs attached to the sign-off logged as tracked actions with owners.
generic.Test population: The submitted sign-off pack and its prerequisite peer, Legal and Compliance reviews.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: Fail if any prerequisite review is incomplete or the sign-off omits the version and date.
generic.Exception handling path: Incomplete prerequisites hold the submission and route back to the Insurance Product Dev Lead.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: Executed CUO sign-off citing the exact coverage design version and date approved.
generic.Evidence location: Sign-off pack and executed sign-off in the SharePoint product governance record.

steps.title: Assemble the sign-off pack in SharePoint
sop: Collect the final coverage terms, limits table, eligibility tiers and endorsement index.
Combine them into one sign-off pack with a contents list on the cover page.
Stamp the pack with the coverage design version number and date.
Done when the versioned sign-off pack is saved in the SharePoint governance folder.
verify: Check each item on the contents list against the attachments in the pack.
Pass when every listed document is present at the stated version.

steps.title: Confirm prerequisite reviews are closed
sop: Check the peer review, Legal review and Compliance review logs for open items.
Record the status of each review on the sign-off pack cover page.
Hold the submission where any review remains open.
Done when all three reviews are recorded as closed on the cover page.
verify: Open each review log and filter for open items.
Pass when no prerequisite review has an open item at submission.

steps.title: Submit the pack to the Chief Underwriting Officer
sop: Send the sign-off pack to the Chief Underwriting Officer with the decision requested stated.
State the exact document version and date being put forward for approval.
Record the submission date in the governance record.
Done when the pack is submitted and the submission date is recorded.
verify: Check the governance record for the submission entry.
Pass when the entry names the version submitted and the date.

steps.title: Obtain the executed CUO signature
sop: Obtain the Chief Underwriting Officer signature on the sign-off sheet.
Confirm the signature block names the exact document version and approval date.
Reject a signature that does not identify the version being approved.
Done when a signed sheet naming the version and date is held.
verify: Read the signature block for the version reference and date.
Pass when both are present and match the submitted pack.

steps.title: Log sign-off conditions as tracked actions
sop: Record any condition or carve-out stated by the CUO as an action.
Assign each action an owner and a due date in the governance action log.
Notify each owner of the condition and the deadline.
Done when every stated condition exists as an owned, dated action.
verify: Compare the CUO conditions against the governance action log.
Pass when every condition has a matching action with owner and due date.

steps.title: File the executed sign-off in the governance record
sop: File the executed sign-off in the document management repository governance record.
Link it to the approved coverage design version.
Apply the retention class used for product governance approvals.
Done when the executed sign-off is filed and linked to the approved version.
verify: Open the approved version record and follow the sign-off link.
Pass when the executed sign-off opens from the version record.

generic.Defined scope/population: The approved coverage design pack, limits table, eligibility tiers and endorsement index.
generic.In-scope period: The version approved by the CUO and being frozen as the baseline for forms and rates.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Published package tagged with product code, version, approval date and CUO sign-off reference.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Published document count matches the approved sign-off pack contents list.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Published package held in the repository with version, approval date and retention class applied.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Draft versions not superseded at publication logged and corrected before the baseline is announced.
generic.Test population: All coverage design documents published to the product repository.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: Fail if any superseded draft is still marked current or any tag field is blank.
generic.Exception handling path: Publication defects route to the Product Development Analyst and hold the baseline notification.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: Approved package published, correctly tagged and drafts superseded before notification.
generic.Evidence location: Product repository publication record and the SharePoint notification to forms and rates leads.

steps.title: Publish the approved package to the product repository
sop: Upload the approved coverage design pack, limits table, eligibility tiers and endorsement index.
Place them in the product repository folder for the product code.
Check each uploaded file opens and is the approved version.
Done when all four approved documents are published to the repository.
verify: Compare the published file list against the sign-off pack contents list.
Pass when every approved document is published.

steps.title: Tag the package with product code, version and approval data
sop: Apply the product code, version number and approval date tags to each published file.
Add the CUO sign-off reference to the package metadata.
Save the metadata and confirm it displays on the repository record.
Done when all four tag fields are populated on the published package.
verify: Open the repository record and read the metadata fields.
Pass when product code, version, approval date and sign-off reference are all populated.

steps.title: Set prior drafts to superseded
sop: List every prior draft of the coverage design in the repository.
Set each prior draft status to superseded.
Confirm the current-document view returns only the approved version.
Done when no prior draft remains retrievable as current.
verify: Query the current-document view for the product code.
Pass when only the approved version is returned.

steps.title: Apply the record retention class
sop: Apply the retention class required for approved product design records.
Confirm the disposition date is calculated by the repository.
Record the retention class on the publication note.
Done when the retention class and disposition date are set on the package.
verify: Open the package properties and read the retention fields.
Pass when the retention class and disposition date are both set.

steps.title: Notify forms drafting and rate development leads
sop: Send the baseline notification to the forms drafting and rate development leads.
State that the baseline is frozen and give the repository link and version.
Ask for acknowledgement of receipt from each lead.
Done when both leads have been notified and have acknowledged.
verify: Check the notification thread for acknowledgements from both leads.
Pass when both acknowledgements are recorded.

steps.title: Record the publication in the governance record
sop: Record the publication date, version and repository location in the governance record.
Link the publication entry to the CUO sign-off entry.
Note the notification recipients on the entry.
Done when the publication entry is complete and linked to the sign-off.
verify: Open the governance record publication entry.
Pass when it names the version, date, location and the sign-off link.

generic.Defined scope/population: The designed coverage features and the plan target loss ratio for the affected line.
generic.In-scope period: The experience and assumption set agreed for the current coverage design version.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Model run records frequency and severity assumptions, modelled loss ratio and target loss ratio.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Modelled exposure and premium in the run reconcile to the design limits and expected mix.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Model run output and signed reconciliation stored in SharePoint with run date and version.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Gaps to target logged with either a proposed design change or an accepted exception.
generic.Test population: All coverage features modelled in the loss ratio reconciliation.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: Fail if a gap to target loss ratio has no design change or accepted exception recorded.
generic.Exception handling path: Unresolved gaps escalate to the Pricing Actuary before the design goes for approval.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: Modelled loss ratio compared to plan target with driver attribution and a signed reconciliation.
generic.Evidence location: Actuarial modelling platform run output and reconciliation file in SharePoint.

steps.title: Agree the frequency and severity assumptions for the model run
sop: Agree the frequency and severity assumptions with the Pricing Actuary.
Record the assumption source and the experience period used.
Save the assumption set into the actuarial modelling platform run definition.
Done when the assumption set is recorded and loaded into the run definition.
verify: Open the run definition and read the assumption set.
Pass when every assumption names a source and an experience period.

steps.title: Model the expected loss ratio of the designed coverage
sop: Run the designed coverage through the actuarial modelling platform on the agreed assumptions.
Capture the modelled expected loss ratio and the underlying premium and loss.
Store the run output with its run date and version reference.
Done when the modelled loss ratio is produced and the run output is stored.
verify: Open the run output and check the loss ratio and its inputs.
Pass when the output shows a modelled loss ratio built on the agreed assumptions.

steps.title: Compare the modelled result to the plan target loss ratio
sop: Retrieve the plan target loss ratio for the line from the SharePoint planning file.
Compare the modelled loss ratio to the target and quantify the gap.
Record both figures and the gap in the reconciliation file.
Done when the gap to plan target is quantified and recorded.
verify: Read the reconciliation file for modelled, target and gap values.
Pass when all three values are present and consistent.

steps.title: Attribute the deviation to coverage features
sop: Re-run the model varying limits, sub-limits and write-backs one at a time.
Rank the coverage features by their contribution to the deviation from target.
Record the driver attribution in the reconciliation file.
Done when the largest deviation drivers are identified and ranked.
verify: Check the attribution table sums to the total deviation within tolerance.
Pass when the attributed drivers explain the modelled gap.

steps.title: Record a design change or an accepted exception for each gap
sop: For each material gap, propose a specific coverage design change to close it.
Where no change is proposed, record the accepted exception and who accepted it.
Route proposed design changes to the Insurance Product Dev Lead.
Done when every material gap carries a design change or an accepted exception.
verify: Filter the gap list for rows with neither a change nor an exception.
Pass when the filter returns no rows.

steps.title: Obtain the pricing owner signature on the reconciliation
sop: Review the reconciliation, attribution and gap dispositions.
Sign and date the reconciliation as the pricing owner.
Store the signed reconciliation in SharePoint against the design version.
Done when the signed reconciliation is stored against the design version.
verify: Open the design version record and locate the signed reconciliation.
Pass when a signed and dated reconciliation is present before design approval.

generic.Defined scope/population: Every clause of the coverage language and every target state whose rules apply to it.
generic.In-scope period: The coverage design version submitted for Legal and Compliance review.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Each finding records clause reference, jurisdiction and the required change.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Findings count in the review record matches the findings raised by both reviewers.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Dated Legal and Compliance sign-off naming the reviewed version held in SharePoint.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Clauses flagged as prohibited wording logged and amended or withdrawn before sign-off.
generic.Test population: All clauses in the reviewed coverage language across all target states.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: Fail if a prohibited clause remains unamended or a finding lacks a jurisdiction.
generic.Exception handling path: Contested findings escalate to Legal Counsel for a final position before sign-off.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: Clause-level findings logged with jurisdiction and change, plus dated Legal and Compliance sign-off.
generic.Evidence location: Review record and sign-off in the SharePoint product design library.

steps.title: Assemble the state mandatory and prohibited wording references
sop: Retrieve the mandatory provision and prohibited wording references for each target state.
Confirm each reference is the current edition from the document management repository.
Save the reference set to the SharePoint review folder for the review.
Done when a current reference set exists for every target state.
verify: Check the reference set against the target state list.
Pass when no target state is missing a current reference.

steps.title: Review the coverage language clause by clause
sop: Read each clause against the mandatory provisions and prohibited wording for each state.
Mark clauses that conflict with a state requirement.
Record the state and the nature of each conflict as you go.
Done when every clause has been read against every target state reference.
verify: Compare the reviewed clause list against the full clause list.
Pass when no clause is left unreviewed.

steps.title: Assess consumer-facing clauses for plain language
sop: Identify the consumer-facing clauses in the coverage language.
Assess each against the plain-language and readability standards for the target states.
Mark clauses requiring a rewrite and note the reason.
Done when every consumer-facing clause carries a plain-language assessment.
verify: Filter the consumer-facing clause list for unassessed rows.
Pass when every consumer-facing clause has an assessment.

steps.title: Check cancellation, non-renewal and notice provisions
sop: Compare the cancellation, non-renewal and notice periods in the wording to each state minimum.
Flag any provision shorter than the statutory minimum for a target state.
Record the required period against each flagged provision.
Done when every notice provision has been checked against each target state minimum.
verify: Read the notice provision table against the state minimum table.
Pass when no provision falls below a target state statutory minimum.

steps.title: Log every finding with clause, jurisdiction and required change
sop: Enter each finding in the review record with clause reference, jurisdiction and required change.
Assign an owner for the amendment against each finding.
Reconcile the logged count against the findings raised by both reviewers.
Done when every finding is logged with all three fields and an owner.
verify: Filter the review record for findings missing a field or owner.
Pass when the filter returns no rows.

steps.title: Record the Legal and Compliance sign-off
sop: Confirm prohibited wording findings have been amended in the reviewed version.
Record dated Legal and Compliance sign-off naming the coverage design version reviewed.
File the sign-off with the review record in SharePoint.
Done when both sign-offs are recorded against the named version.
verify: Open the sign-off and read the version reference and date.
Pass when both sign-offs name the reviewed version and are dated.

generic.Defined scope/population: The underwriting guidelines document and the named owner and deputy accountable for it.
generic.In-scope period: The appointment taking effect from the recorded date of acceptance.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Owner name, role, appointment date, deputy name and written acceptance are all recorded.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Register entry for the guidelines matches the named owner and deputy on the acceptance record.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Dated written acceptance filed against the guidelines entry in the document register.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Periods with no named owner or deputy logged and closed by an interim appointment.
generic.Test population: The guidelines register entry and the access rights on the published guidelines.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: Fail if the owner or deputy is unnamed or any other user holds edit rights.
generic.Exception handling path: Unfilled ownership escalates to the Insurance Product Manager for an immediate appointment.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: Named owner and deputy recorded with acceptance date and owner-only edit rights confirmed.
generic.Evidence location: Guidelines entry in the document register and the SharePoint permissions record.

steps.title: Name the accountable guidelines owner
sop: Select the individual accountable for the underwriting guidelines content and review cadence.
Record the individual's name, role and date of appointment.
Confirm the appointment with the Insurance Product Manager.
Done when the owner name, role and appointment date are recorded.
verify: Read the appointment record for the three fields.
Pass when name, role and appointment date are all populated.

steps.title: Capture the owner's written acceptance
sop: Send the owner a statement of the responsibility for content accuracy and review cadence.
Obtain written acceptance from the owner in reply.
File the acceptance in SharePoint with the date received.
Done when a dated written acceptance is filed.
verify: Open the filed acceptance and check the date and signatory.
Pass when the acceptance is dated and from the named owner.

steps.title: Name a deputy to cover absence
sop: Name a deputy who takes the guidelines ownership during the owner's absence.
Confirm the deputy accepts the cover arrangement.
Record the deputy name against the guidelines entry.
Done when a named deputy is recorded and has accepted.
verify: Read the guidelines entry for the deputy name and acceptance.
Pass when a deputy is named and the acceptance is recorded.

steps.title: Enter the owner in the document register
sop: Open the guidelines record in the document register in the repository.
Enter the owner, deputy and appointment date against the record.
Save the entry and confirm it displays on the register view.
Done when the register shows the owner and deputy against the guidelines.
verify: Query the register for the guidelines record.
Pass when the returned entry names the owner and deputy.

steps.title: Set owner-only edit rights on the published guidelines
sop: Review the SharePoint permissions on the published guidelines library.
Grant edit rights to the owner and deputy only.
Set all other users to read-only access.
Done when only the owner and deputy hold edit rights.
verify: Export the permissions list for the published guidelines.
Pass when no user other than the owner and deputy has edit rights.

steps.title: Notify stakeholders of the ownership arrangement
sop: Notify underwriting, compliance and operations of the named owner and deputy.
State how change requests to the guidelines should be routed to the owner.
File the notification with the appointment record.
Done when the notification is issued and filed.
verify: Check the appointment record for the filed notification.
Pass when the notification names the owner, deputy and routing path.

generic.Defined scope/population: Every affected line of business and its senior underwriter and line leadership reviewers.
generic.In-scope period: The draft guidelines version circulated at least one week before the review session.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Each comment records the guidelines section, commenter, disposition and edit owner.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Comments logged per section match the comments returned by the circulated reviewers.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Review log and line leadership confirmation stored in SharePoint with the draft version and date.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Challenges to authority thresholds and referral triggers logged separately with a decision.
generic.Test population: All comments raised across the appetite, eligibility, authority, referral and pricing sections.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: Fail if any affected line lacks a named reviewer or any comment lacks a disposition and owner.
generic.Exception handling path: Unresolved authority or referral challenges escalate to the Insurance Product Dev Lead.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: Comments captured per section with disposition and owner plus line leadership workability confirmation.
generic.Evidence location: Guidelines peer review log in the SharePoint underwriting guidelines folder.

steps.title: Circulate the draft guidelines a week before review
sop: Save the versioned draft guidelines to the SharePoint review folder.
Send the link to senior underwriters and line leadership for every affected line.
Circulate at least one week before the review session and record the send date.
Done when the draft is circulated to every affected line with the lead time met.
verify: Compare the send date to the session date and the recipient list to the affected lines.
Pass when every affected line was sent the draft at least one week ahead.

steps.title: Run the review section by section
sop: Take the session through appetite, eligibility, authority, referral and pricing guidance in order.
Invite comments on each section before moving to the next.
Log comments against the section they relate to as they are raised.
Done when all five sections have been reviewed and their comments logged.
verify: Check the log for comments recorded against each of the five sections.
Pass when every section shows a completed review entry.

steps.title: Capture challenges to authority thresholds and referral triggers
sop: Record every challenge to an authority threshold or referral trigger as its own log entry.
Note the current value, the proposed value and the reviewer raising it.
Mark these entries as system-impacting so configuration sees them.
Done when every threshold and trigger challenge is logged with current and proposed values.
verify: Filter the log for threshold and trigger entries missing a proposed value.
Pass when the filter returns no rows.

steps.title: Disposition each comment with rationale and owner
sop: Mark each comment accepted or rejected with a written rationale.
Assign an owner to every resulting edit with a due date.
Return rejections to the reviewer who raised them.
Done when every comment has a disposition, rationale and owner where accepted.
verify: Filter the log for comments with no disposition or no edit owner.
Pass when the filter returns no rows.

steps.title: Obtain line leadership workability confirmation
sop: Ask line leadership to confirm the guidelines are workable in day-to-day submission handling.
Record any operational concern raised as a log entry with an owner.
Obtain the confirmation in writing from each affected line.
Done when written workability confirmation is held for every affected line.
verify: Check the confirmation set against the affected lines list.
Pass when every affected line has provided written confirmation.

steps.title: Close the review log and hand it to the revision step
sop: Reconcile the log against the comments returned by every reviewer.
Save the completed log against the reviewed draft version in SharePoint.
Hand the log to the owner of the guidelines revision step.
Done when the reconciled log is saved against the reviewed version and handed over.
verify: Open the reviewed version record and locate the review log.
Pass when the log is attached and reconciled to the reviewer returns.

generic.Defined scope/population: Every mandatory submission field, supporting document and risk question for the new product.
generic.In-scope period: The submission requirements version issued to policy system configuration.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Each requirement names the field, answer format and whether it is mandatory or knock-out.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Rating variables in the rating plan all map to an application question one for one.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Versioned submission requirements document dated in the SharePoint product design library.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Fields Operations cannot capture in the policy system intake screen logged with an agreed alternative.
generic.Test population: All submission fields, supporting documents and risk questions in the requirements document.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: Fail if any rating variable has no application question or any driver question is free text.
generic.Exception handling path: Uncapturable fields route to the Insurance Product Dev Lead for redesign or removal.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: Every mandatory requirement and rating variable has a defined capture field and answer format.
generic.Evidence location: Submission requirements document in SharePoint and the intake screen spec in the policy system.

steps.title: List the mandatory submission fields and documents
sop: List the fields and supporting documents without which a submission is incomplete.
Record each as a row in the requirements document in SharePoint.
Mark each row mandatory or optional.
Done when every mandatory submission item appears as a marked row.
verify: Filter the requirements table for rows with no mandatory or optional marking.
Pass when the filter returns no rows.

steps.title: Map every rating variable to an application question
sop: List every rating variable in the rating plan.
Map each variable to the specific application question that collects it.
Raise any variable with no question so a question can be written.
Done when every rating variable names its collecting question.
verify: Compare the rating variable list against the mapped questions.
Pass when no rating variable is left without an application question.

steps.title: Define answer formats for rating and eligibility questions
sop: Give each question that drives rating or eligibility a coded list or numeric range answer format.
Remove free-text formats from any question that feeds a rule or a factor.
Record the permitted values against each question.
Done when no rating or eligibility question uses a free-text answer format.
verify: Filter the question list for free-text answers on rating or eligibility questions.
Pass when the filter returns no rows.

steps.title: Specify the knock-out questions
sop: Identify the questions whose answers trigger automatic declination or referral.
State the triggering answer value and the resulting outcome for each.
Mark these questions as knock-out in the requirements document.
Done when every knock-out question states its trigger value and outcome.
verify: Read the knock-out list for trigger values and outcomes.
Pass when every knock-out question has both recorded.

steps.title: Confirm capture feasibility on the policy system intake screen
sop: Walk the required fields through the policy administration system intake screen with Operations.
Record confirmation that each field can be captured as specified.
Log fields that cannot be captured with the agreed alternative treatment.
Done when every required field has a capture confirmation or a logged alternative.
verify: Filter the field list for rows with no capture confirmation.
Pass when every field is confirmed capturable or has a logged alternative.

steps.title: Version and issue the submission requirements
sop: Increment the requirements document version and date it.
Issue it to configuration, underwriting and the actuarial team.
Record the issue in the SharePoint product design library.
Done when the versioned requirements are issued and recorded.
verify: Open the library record for the issued version.
Pass when the issued version is dated and its recipients are recorded.

generic.Defined scope/population: Every named segment and its target profile, eligibility and mandatory declination criteria.
generic.In-scope period: The criteria version going into the approved underwriting guidelines.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Each declination criterion states a testable attribute, operator and threshold value.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Segment count in the criteria tables matches the segment list in the product specification.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Versioned criteria tables dated and stored in the document management repository.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Conflicts with the enterprise no-write list logged and resolved before the guidelines issue.
generic.Test population: All eligibility and declination criteria across all named segments and target states.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: Fail if a declination reason is impermissible in a target state or requires underwriter judgement.
generic.Exception handling path: Appetite exception candidates route to the defined referral path rather than automatic declination.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: Target profile, eligibility and mandatory declination criteria stated for every named segment.
generic.Evidence location: Criteria tables in the document management repository underwriting guidelines folder.

steps.title: State target profile and eligibility per named segment
sop: Create one criteria block per named segment in the guidelines draft.
State the target risk profile and the eligibility criteria separately in each block.
Keep the wording testable rather than descriptive.
Done when every named segment has its own target profile and eligibility criteria.
verify: Compare the criteria blocks against the segment list in the product specification.
Pass when every named segment has a block with both elements.

steps.title: Express declination criteria as unambiguous tests
sop: Write each mandatory declination criterion as an attribute, operator and threshold.
Use class code, loss history threshold or exposure limit rather than descriptive language.
Remove any criterion that needs underwriter judgement to apply.
Done when every declination criterion is applicable without judgement.
verify: Read each criterion and try to apply it to a sample risk without interpretation.
Pass when every criterion returns a clear decline or pass on the sample.

steps.title: Reconcile declinations against the enterprise no-write list
sop: Retrieve the enterprise no-write and prohibited-risk lists from the repository.
Compare the declination criteria against both lists for conflicts and gaps.
Resolve each conflict by amending the criteria or escalating the appetite question.
Done when no conflict remains between the criteria and the enterprise lists.
verify: Re-run the comparison against the current list version.
Pass when no criterion conflicts with the enterprise no-write list.

steps.title: Check declination reasons against state rules
sop: Compare each declination reason against unfair-discrimination and permissible-declination rules per target state.
Flag reasons that are impermissible or restricted in any target state.
Amend or state-limit each flagged reason and record the decision.
Done when every declination reason has been checked in every target state.
verify: Re-check the amended reasons against the state rule references.
Pass when no declination reason is impermissible in a target state.

steps.title: Define the appetite exception referral path
sop: Define the referral path for risks that fail eligibility but merit an appetite exception.
Name the authority level that can grant the exception and the evidence required.
Record the path in the guidelines alongside the eligibility criteria.
Done when the referral path, authority and evidence requirements are documented.
verify: Read the referral path section for authority level and evidence requirements.
Pass when both are stated and consistent with the authority matrix.

steps.title: Version and file the criteria tables
sop: Increment the criteria tables version and stamp them with the date.
File them in the underwriting guidelines folder in the repository.
Notify the guidelines owner that the criteria are ready for inclusion.
Done when the versioned criteria tables are filed and notified.
verify: Open the guidelines folder and locate the versioned criteria tables.
Pass when the current version is present and dated.

generic.Defined scope/population: Net retention, treaty limit and facultative referral triggers for every coverage part.
generic.In-scope period: The in-force treaty period stated on the current treaty slip.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Each coverage part records retention, treaty limit and numeric facultative referral triggers.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Retention figures in the guidance match the figures in the in-force treaty slip.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Versioned reinsurance guidance dated and filed with the treaty slip reference in the repository.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Retention or trigger values that differ from the treaty logged and corrected before issue.
generic.Test population: All coverage parts and their retention and facultative referral guidance.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: Fail if a retention figure exceeds the treaty slip limit or a trigger is descriptive not numeric.
generic.Exception handling path: Treaty conflicts escalate to the Product / Filing Actuary before the guidance is issued.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: Numeric retention limits and facultative referral triggers stated per coverage part.
generic.Evidence location: Reinsurance guidance section in the SharePoint underwriting guidelines draft.

steps.title: State net retention and treaty limit per coverage part
sop: State the net retention for each coverage part in the guidance section.
State the treaty limit above which business must be ceded for each coverage part.
Record both as numeric values rather than descriptive guidance.
Done when every coverage part shows a numeric retention and treaty limit.
verify: Filter the guidance table for coverage parts missing either figure.
Pass when the filter returns no rows.

steps.title: Set numeric facultative referral triggers
sop: Set the facultative referral triggers on limit, total insured value, hazard class and aggregation zone.
Express each trigger as a numeric threshold with the unit stated.
Remove any descriptive trigger wording from the guidance.
Done when every referral trigger is numeric with its unit stated.
verify: Read each trigger for a numeric threshold and a unit.
Pass when no trigger is left as descriptive guidance.

steps.title: Reconcile retention figures to the in-force treaty slip
sop: Retrieve the current treaty slip from the document management repository.
Compare each stated retention against the treaty slip wording.
Note the treaty expiry date in the guidance so the review is diarised.
Done when every retention reconciles to the slip and the expiry date is recorded.
verify: Re-read the slip against the guidance retention table.
Pass when no retention figure exceeds the limit in the in-force slip.

steps.title: Define who may bind subject to facultative
sop: Name the authority level that may bind a risk subject to facultative placement.
State the evidence required from the reinsurer before the risk is bound.
Record the rule alongside the referral triggers.
Done when the binding authority and required evidence are documented.
verify: Read the subject-to-facultative rule for authority and evidence requirements.
Pass when both are explicitly stated.

steps.title: Add the coinsurance and maximum line guidance
sop: State the maximum line the company will write on a shared placement.
Set out the coinsurance guidance including any minimum participation.
Check the maximum line is consistent with the stated net retention.
Done when the coinsurance guidance and maximum line are documented and consistent.
verify: Compare the maximum line against the retention figures.
Pass when the maximum line sits within the stated retention.

steps.title: Version and file the reinsurance guidance section
sop: Increment the guidance version and date it with the treaty slip reference.
File the section into the underwriting guidelines draft in the repository.
Notify the guidelines owner that the section is complete.
Done when the versioned section is filed into the guidelines draft.
verify: Open the guidelines draft and locate the reinsurance section.
Pass when the current version is present with the treaty reference.

generic.Defined scope/population: The full risk classification tier set and every eligible risk profile it must classify.
generic.In-scope period: The historical exposure period used to test tier credibility.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Each tier records qualifying criteria, numeric boundaries and the rating engine code.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Tier codes in the guidelines match the codes configured in Earnix Rating and Pricing.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Versioned tier definition table dated in SharePoint with the credibility test output attached.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Tiers with insufficient exposure volume logged and merged or supported by a stated complement.
generic.Test population: All tier definitions and a sample of risk profiles spanning the tier boundaries.
generic.Pass/fail thresholds: Fail if a risk profile maps to zero tiers or to more than one tier.
generic.Exception handling path: Boundary-straddling and missing-data risks follow the documented default tier treatment.
generic.Documented acceptance criteria: Mutually exclusive and exhaustive tiers with numeric boundaries and rating engine codes.
generic.Evidence location: Tier definition table in SharePoint and the tier code list in Earnix Rating and Pricing.

steps.title: Define each tier with criteria and numeric boundaries
sop: Define each risk classification tier with its qualifying criteria.
State the numeric boundary between each tier and the adjacent tier.
Record the definitions in the tier table in SharePoint.
Done when every tier has qualifying criteria and numeric boundaries.
verify: Read the boundary values from the lowest tier to the highest.
Pass when every tier has criteria and adjoining boundary values.

steps.title: Test the tier set for exclusivity and exhaustiveness
sop: Build a sample of risk profiles spanning the boundaries and the extremes.
Apply the tier criteria to each profile and record the tiers it matches.
Amend criteria where a profile matches none or more than one tier.
Done when every sample profile maps to exactly one tier.
verify: Count the matched tiers per sample profile.
Pass when every profile returns exactly one tier.

steps.title: Check each tier has credible exposure volume
sop: Extract historical exposure volume by proposed tier for the agreed period.
Compare each tier volume against the credibility standard.
Merge or support tiers that fall below the standard and record the treatment.
Done when every tier meets the credibility standard or carries a stated complement.
verify: Read the volume table against the credibility standard.
Pass when no tier is left below standard without a stated complement.

steps.title: Align tier names and codes with the rating engine
sop: Agree the tier code values to be configured in Earnix Rating and Pricing.
Record the code against each tier in the tier table.
Confirm with pricing that the codes match the planned rating plan structure.
Done when every tier carries the agreed rating engine code.
verify: Compare the tier codes in the table against the Earnix rating plan structure.
Pass when the code sets match exactly.

steps.title: Document boundary-straddling and missing-data treatment
sop: State how a risk sitting exactly on a boundary is classified.
State the default tier or referral treatment where classification data is missing.
Record both rules with the tier definitions.
Done when boundary and missing-data treatments are documented.
verify: Apply the rules to a boundary case and a missing-data case.
Pass when each case resolves to a single defined outcome.

steps.title: Version and issue the tier definitions
sop: Increment the tier table version and date it.
Issue it into the underwriting guidelines and to the rating plan owner.
Record the issue in the SharePoint guidelines folder.
Done when the versioned tier table is issued to both destinations.
verify: Check the guidelines folder and the rating plan input record.
Pass when both hold the same tier table version.

generic.Defined scope/population: Schedule rating categories, deviation tolerances and decision rules for every authority level.
generic.In-scope period: The filed rate rules version currently in force for the product.
generic.Required fields populated and valid: Each category records maximum credit, maximum debit and the file documentation required.
generic.Control totals or record counts reconcil: Guidance deviation ranges reconcile to the maxima in the filed rate rules.
generic.Evidence retained with timestamp/version: Versioned pricing guidance section dated in SharePoint with the filed rule reference.
generic.Exceptions logged with disposition: Any tolerance exceeding the filed maximum logged and reduced before the guidance is issued.
